# Pre-registered analysis plan, stage 7: tuning parity, scope and ablations

**Fixed on:** 14 November 2026 (Asia/Kuala_Lumpur), before any stage-7 run.
**Do not edit this file.** `compare_best.py --plan` records its SHA-256. Later additions go in a separate, dated addendum.

## Status of the data
All four test sets have been examined:
- UNSW main (9–10 October 2016);
- UNSW split 2 (27 September 2016);
- Deakin main (21 April 2024);
- Deakin split 2 (4 April 2024).

This round is therefore **not** a confirmation on unseen data. It tests whether the paper's central claim survives tuning of the learned models and changes of window length, prediction horizon, history length and class weighting. Every rule below is fixed before any of these runs.

## Claim under test
On each test set, two methods are compared, both chosen on validation data only:
- **S\***, the best simple method: one of Persistence, Recent frequency (L = 4), Transition, EWMA (L = 4), EWMA (expanding) and History-LR. It is the one with the highest validation macro F1 at its exact validation threshold.
- **M\***, the best learned model: the one with the highest mean validation macro F1 over its five seeds.

At the validation edge budget, two counts are compared per test window:
- *edges right*: true positives;
- *changes recovered*: new edges predicted plus disappearing edges not predicted.

M\* − S\* is estimated with the two-level paired bootstrap: seeds plus 8-window circular moving blocks within each capture, 10,000 replicates, two-sided p-values. Holm adjustment covers the 8 contrasts of a setting (4 test sets × 2 measures). With margin m = 0.5 edges per window, each test set is classified as one of:
- **learned clearly better:** one measure favours M\* (difference > 0, Holm p < 0.05) and the other is not worse by more than m (lower 95% bound > −m);
- **simple clearly better:** the mirror image of the rule above;
- **trade-off:** both of the above hold;
- **no clear winner:** neither holds.

The claim is that **learned models are not reliably better: M\* is clearly better on at most 1 of the 4 test sets.** The `default` setting (existing runs) is reported as the reference. It is exploratory, because its results have been seen.

## Settings and predictions
Each prediction holds if the learned model is clearly better on at most 1 of the 4 test sets, unless stated otherwise.

| ID | Setting | Learned models (candidates for M\*) | Prediction |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | **7A tuned.** Each model gets 4 settings: the published setting; learning rate 3e-4; widths × 0.5; widths × 2. Seed 42 of each; the highest validation F1 wins (ties: validation AP, then the default). The winner is trained with seeds 42–46 (`tune_models.py`). | DynGEM, AERNN, VGRNN, TGAE, VRDAG, Static VGAE (previous window), asymmetric TGAE | at most 1 of 4 |
| P2a, P2b | **7B window length:** 600 s and 900 s windows, made by merging 2 or 3 consecutive 300 s windows (`make_merged_windows.py`). Simple methods are recomputed and History-LR is refitted on the merged data. | TGAE, asymmetric TGAE, VRDAG, each with its 7A setting | at most 1 of 4, each |
| P3a, P3b | **7C horizon:** predict 2 and 4 windows ahead (10 and 20 minutes) instead of 1. Implementation to follow; see below. | as 7B | at most 1 of 4, each |
| P4a, P4b | **7D history length:** learned models see only the last 1 or 2 history windows; simple methods unchanged (`run_scope.py`). | as 7B | at most 1 of 4, each |
| P5 | **7E class weighting off:** TGAE, VGRNN and Static VGAE (previous window), published setting, unweighted loss (`run_scope.py --setting noweight`). | n/a | For all 3 models on all 4 test sets, mean edges predicted at 0.5 are at least 10 × the observed edges. The floor comes from the bias-free inner-product decoder, not from the class weight. |

**Horizon (7C) procedure, fixed now:**
- History windows t−4 … t−1, target window t+h−1 (h = 2, 4).
- Models, tuned settings and decoders are as in 7B. Persistence, Recent frequency and EWMA (L = 4) use the same four history windows.
- Transition, and History-LR's transition feature, are refitted on h-step transitions in the training data. EWMA (expanding) uses only windows up to t−1.
- The validation budget is the mean edge count of the validation targets. The "previous window" in the definitions of new and disappearing edges is window t−1.
- The implementing script is added, with its hash, in an addendum before any horizon run.

**Descriptive, with no prediction:**
- which setting wins in 7A for each model and test set;
- tuned against default validation and test results;
- History-LR's chosen C on the merged data;
- the identity checks recorded by `make_merged_windows.py`.

## Order, completeness and reporting
- **Run order:** 7A, 7B, 7C, 7E, 7D, as far as the available computer allows.
- **Completeness:** a setting is evaluated only when it is complete on all four test sets. A setting that cannot be completed is reported as not run, never partially.
- **Reporting:** every prediction that is run is reported, whatever its outcome.
- **Deviations:** any change to a script or command after this plan is fixed is recorded as a deviation, with its reason.
